findings.title: `skills uninstall --commands-dir` "must match the receipt destination" cannot hold for Claude receipts
findings.description:
The contract says `--commands-dir` on uninstall is a check against the receipt's destination, exiting 1 with nothing removed on a mismatch. The slice's own reading of the receipt is wrong for Claude packs.
- For Claude packs, `_install_prefix` records `destination = commands_dir/<prefix>` (`installer.py:83,91`). `_install_dispatch` records `commands_dir/sq` (`installer.py:103`). Neither is the root the flag names.
- The existing uninstall tests pass `--commands-dir <root>`: `test_cli_skills.py:107-194` (round trip, unrelated file, idempotent). Those receipts hold `<root>/analysis`, so a strict comparison exits 1 and all three tests fail.
- Today `skills uninstall` ignores `--commands-dir` entirely; it only uses `receipt.destination` (`skills.py:95,110`). Making it a hard check breaks existing scripts too.
- Line 184 and criterion 6 (line 226) promise that no-flag and existing behavior is unchanged. This contradicts both.

Drop the check for `skills uninstall`, or compare against the install root (receipt destination, or its parent for Claude). State which, and which existing tests change.

findings.title: Agents uninstall can remove `~/.agents/skills` itself; the receipt `surface` for agents installs is never specified
findings.description:
The data flow says `remove_receipt_files` never removes the destination. It also says "for a Claude prefix pack the now-empty prefix directory is still removed, as today." That rmdir lives in `skills.py:120-122`. It fires on `receipt.surface == PREFIX` and removes `destination` when it is empty.
- An agents receipt's destination is the shared root (data flow, line 97).
- If the agents receipt carries `surface=PREFIX`, which `_write_install_receipt` derives from `entry.prefix` (`installer.py:50`), uninstalling the last skill would `rmdir ~/.agents/skills`. That violates criterion 2 (line 222).
- Walkthrough step 5 (line 269) hides this by leaving `mine.txt` in the directory.

Specify the surface for agents receipts (`None`) and gate the prefix-dir removal on the Claude target. Add a test where the root empties.

findings.title: Receipt-name refactor breaks existing `test_targets.py` tests and is under-specified at `install_pack`
findings.description:
Line 184 says existing tests pass "without edits other than the moved fixture paths". That is false.
- `tests/skills/test_targets.py:58` reads `receipt_base`, which D5 renames to `receipt_suffix`.
- `test_targets.py:62-74` calls `receipt_name(target, local=)`, which becomes `receipt_name(base, target, *, local)`.
- There are 14+ existing `install_pack("mypack", entry, commands_dir[, receipts_dir])` calls (`test_installer.py`). The new `target` parameter must default to Claude.

Two gaps remain in the install path:
- The component table gives `install_pack(..., target)` no `local`, but the receipt name needs the scope (D5).
- `write_receipt` names the file from `receipt.pack_name` (`receipts.py:39`). For an agents receipt, `pack_name` must therefore carry `analysis-agents[-local]`, as `install_for_target` does. `InstallResult.pack_name` is also printed to the user as the pack name (`skills.py:77`).

Say where the suffixed name lives, add `local` to the signature, and list the test edits.

findings.title: The D4 move breaks the agents-tree bijection tests and silently drops coverage of the moved skills
findings.description:
The Migration Plan calls the consumers "fixtures". In `tests/cli/test_install_commands.py:478-580`, `_agents_root()` returns the single directory `commands/agents` and drives five structural tests.
- `test_every_claude_command_has_an_agents_twin` (line 512) iterates the CLAUDE `bundle_subdirs`, including `analysis`. It expects `commands/agents/analysis-understand/SKILL.md`, which no longer exists after the move, so it fails.
- The name, description, `openai.yaml` and no-substitution tests (lines 532-580) iterate `commands/agents` only. After the move, `analysis-*` is no longer covered by any of them.

State that `_agents_root` becomes the set of AGENTS `bundle_subdirs`, and that the bijection is checked across all of them.

findings.title: Agents install status via `p-*` glob gives false "Installed" and ignores the receipt-as-authority principle
findings.description:
For a prefix pack, `installed_path` on the agents target is "first `root/p-*/SKILL.md`". `~/.agents/skills` is shared with every other skill source.
- Any unrelated `analysis-foo` skill makes the `analysis` pack read as installed in `skills list` and in doctor.
- Short prefixes match even more.
- The design's own D3 rationale (line 123) and Patterns (line 176, "receipts remain the only authority") argue against this.
- The existing `test_agents_check_ignores_third_party_skills` (`test_doctor_checks.py:138`) was written for exactly this false OK.

For agents, base status on the receipt, or on the receipt's recorded files.

findings.title: Doctor's "pack ships no Codex content" needs source resolution that doctor does not do, and the hint rule contradicts itself
findings.description:
D8 has doctor report `WARN — pack ships no Codex content`, with no install hint. Doctor cannot know that without resolving the pack source, and `installed_path` (lines 104-109) only checks install state.
- `check_skill_packs` is documented as pure, reading only the manifest and filesystem (`doctor_checks.py:432-435`).
- For `github:` sources, resolving means `git clone` (`resolver.py:61`) on every `sq doctor` run.
- For relative sources it means path resolution against the config dir.
- The design gives no behavior for an unresolvable source or a github pack. The "no hint because it would fail" rule cannot be applied to a pack whose content is unknown.
- `commands_dir` is an existing parameter (`doctor_checks.py:429`). Its meaning across two targets is not stated, and the agents root is not parameterized.
- Walkthrough step 7 (line 279) only exercises a local source.

Proportionality: per-target doctor rows go beyond the plan's Part A (`install`/`uninstall`, line 454) and bring in this I/O path. Either defer them, or restrict the "no Codex content" state to local and bundled sources. Use "not installed" for the rest, and name what the hint says.

findings.title: New receipt-name collisions across packs and across projects are excluded only for squadron's own names
findings.description:
D5 builds the receipt name as `pack + suffix + ("-local")`. Pack names are free-form manifest keys, so `-agents` and `-local` are ambiguous.
- Pack `foo` installed with `--ide codex` and pack `foo-agents` installed for Claude both write `foo-agents.toml`.
- Pack `foo` installed with `--local` and pack `foo-local` both write `foo-local.toml`.

Claude `--local` for skills is new in this slice, so this is not the pre-existing collision that line 52 excludes. That exclusion covers only "squadron's own receipt names or skill names".

Local receipts are also one file per scope under `~/.config`, not per project. Installing the same pack `--local` in two projects overwrites the first record, and `skills uninstall --local` run from project A then deletes project B's files, because the receipt holds an absolute destination. `install-commands` accepts the same limit. A new skills surface should either reject colliding names at install, or document the limit.

findings.title: The rule's contents are left to implementation, and the probe table omits commands that reach providers or the network
findings.description:
D9 and criterion 8 depend on D10's subcommand list. D10's table leaves `review`, `run`, `metrology`, `skills install`, the daemon commands and `auth login` as "confirm by probe" or "probe". Probing at implementation time is reasonable, but the rule grants unsandboxed execution (line 153), so the candidate set has to be complete.
- The table is not exhaustive against `cli/app.py:47-70`. It omits `sq summary` and the hidden `_summary-instructions`, `_summary-run` and `_dispatch-run`. `commands/agents/sq-summary/SKILL.md:29-70` invokes `sq _summary-instructions`.
- It also omits `doctor`, `setup`, `config`, `pools`, `events` and `serve`.
- D12 adds the sandbox hint to only `sq-review`, `sq-run` and `sq-pr`. If any other probed command lands in the rule, its skill has no hint.

Either complete the enumeration, or state the rule that decides membership and who owns the omitted commands.

findings.title: Failure and sequencing states of the agents install are not enumerated
findings.description:
"Nothing written" holds only for validation failures (lines 94-95). The write is `write_skill_dirs` (copytree), followed by the receipt.
- If copytree fails partway (permissions, disk full), partial skill directories exist and no receipt does. `skills uninstall` then says "not installed", and `list` and doctor report "Installed" from the glob.
- A kill between the write and the receipt leaves the same state.
- A receipt-write failure only logs a WARNING (`installer.py:57-66`). For nested skill directories, that means uninstall can never remove them.
- On reinstall after a pack drops a skill, the new receipt lists only the current files. The old skill directory is orphaned permanently. `install_for_target` handles this by diffing the previous receipt, and `install_pack` has no such step. With multi-file skill directories this is more likely than on the Claude path.

State how each state recovers, or that it is accepted.

findings.title: Proportionality: the `PACK_LAYOUTS` module and the bundled-pack move carry more mechanism than the two-target slice needs
findings.description:
The slice plan assigns effort 2/5 for Part A plus docs, and the design raises it to 3/5. Three pieces can be cut or reduced.
- A new `pack_layouts.py` with a `PackLayout` dataclass and an exhaustiveness assertion is justified by "a new target is a new entry" (D6). The slice excludes every other target (`copilot`, `cursor`, line 51). Two functions next to `install_pack`, plus `installed_path` in `targets.py`, deliver the same behavior.
- D4's move of the bundled skills forces edits to `bundle_subdirs`, `bundled_skill_names`, the fixtures and the bijection tests (see the bijection finding). The aim is "no bundled special case", but the install path is unchanged either way. Weigh the cost against a filter at resolve time before committing to it.
- Per-target doctor rows (see the doctor finding).

findings.title: Verification walkthrough is macOS-only, and the `model list` fix touches six lines
findings.description:
- `sed -i ''` is BSD-only, so step 4 fails on GNU sed.
- The Overview and criterion 9 describe the `sq model list` fix as "one line each" (line 24). In fact `commands/sq/review.md:60,112,158` and `commands/agents/sq-review/SKILL.md:82,134,180` each contain three occurrences, six edits in total.
- The `sq models list` command does exist (`app.py:55`).

findings.title: Alignment with the slice plan entry and with slice 925
findings.description:
The design delivers both plan parts (#125 and #127). It answers the plan's two open questions: a pack-format declaration instead of refusing `$ARGUMENTS` (D2), and no doctor check for the rule (D11, with a reason).
- Dependency direction is correct (CLI to `skills` to `targets`).
- `DELIVERIES`, `write_skill_dirs`, `normalize_target` and `_command_targets_to_check` exist as described.
- The bundled-pack resolution claim holds: `_resolve_bundled("analysis")` returns `commands/analysis`.
- The Claude glob claim holds: `write_flat_markdown` and `_install_prefix` glob `*.md` at the top level, so a new `analysis/agents` subdirectory is invisible to them.
- Wheel packaging force-includes the whole `commands` directory (`pyproject.toml:68-69`).
